title: Waaree Energies Ltd - 544277 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Waaree Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.9% YoY to Rs 7,517.7 crore, with operating EBITDA of Rs 1,335.2 crore (17.8% margin); FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs 7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 7,517.7 crore (up 23.9% YoY) with operating EBITDA of Rs 1,335.2 crore and PAT of Rs 753.6 crore. H1 revenue rose 47.3% to Rs 15,449.5 crore, but H1 PAT was flat at Rs 1,645.5 crore versus Rs 1,651.1 crore a year earlier. Management said the US export order book was rationalised after Section 232 minimum import prices, cutting export share of the order book from about 24% to 7.8%, while retail and US-manufactured volumes grew. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance and expects H2 to deliver 55-60% of it, driven by cell and US capacity ramp-ups.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 margin was 18.2% per analyst; Q1 included US duty refund

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 3,464 crore, 46.1% of Q2 revenue

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 2,875 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 59,200 crore; module order book 25.6 GW
financial_highlights.change: geography: 48.4% domestic India, 43.8% domestic US, 7.8% exports

segments.name: Retail / cash-and-carry (India)
segments.commentary: Q2 retail revenue about Rs 3,464 crore (46.1% of Q2 revenue), up 252% YoY; 775+ exclusive retail centres and about 3,000 distribution points. FY27 retail revenue guided at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore; over 92% of retail revenue is modules.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: 18.5% of Q2 revenue (Rs 1,389 crore vs Rs 2,875 crore a year ago). Within it, US domestic revenue rose to Rs 1,300 crore from Rs 732 crore; exports from India fell to Rs 89 crore from Rs 2,143 crore.

segments.name: EPC, O&M, T&D, others
segments.commentary: Combined 12.6% of Q2 revenue. T&D acquisition sits under the listed subsidiary, which runs a blended EBITDA margin of about 14-15%.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: Domestic US manufacturing revenue up 113% YoY in H1 FY27; US module output reached 0.3 GW in the period at 71% annualised utilisation. Q2 US supply about 400 MW, of which about 300 MW self-manufactured.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance reaffirmed at Rs 7,000-7,700 crore; H1 was about Rs 2,775 crore, so H2 needs about 55-60% of the guided total per management.
Q3 and Q4 volumes expected to be heavy, with 5 GW of Indian cell capacity going live in Q3 and another 5 GW in Q4.
US 1.6 GW module line to become operational in Q3 FY27; a second 1.6 GW line in the next quarter, taking Waaree Solar Americas to 4.8 GW.
Retail revenue guided at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore for FY27.
Newer businesses (BESS, transformers, inverters, T&D, EPC, electrolysers) expected to rise from 15-20% of revenue to 30-35% over 2-3 years; long-range solar 50-60% of revenue.
Management's ambition is Rs 90,000-1 lakh crore revenue over 4-5 years (about 20 GW module output at 75% utilisation plus non-solar businesses); no timeline firmly committed.
capex_capacity: Capex programme about Rs 30,000 crore: 35% deployed, 28% under execution, 37% in planning. Management says cash balance covers under-construction projects without new borrowing.
Installed module capacity 25.8 GW, including 1.6 GW in the US; India cell capacity 5.4 GW rising to 15.4 GW with the 10 GW Unn expansion (cell-to-module ratio from about 22% to about 65%).

Ingot-wafer: 10 GW facility at Nagpur, commercial production targeted September 2027; capex about Rs 5,500 crore per management (analyst cited Rs 6,200-6,500 crore). Ingot-wafer civil works about 70% complete.

BESS: 5.1 GWh container and 5.1 GWh pack Phase 1 (container commissioned in Q2; pack expected in Q3; 3.5 GWh cell pilot from Q4 FY27). Phase 2 (16.5 GWh cell, 15 GWh container) is in planning; funding tied to policy clarity and overseas orders.

Inverter capacity 4 GW (production started); transformer capacity 20,000 MVA with incremental capacity by March 2027; electrolyser capacity also coming. Combined committed capital about Rs 1,200 crore.
Solar glass: about Rs 3,900 crore budget, about Rs 360 crore spent (land, filling, EOP); location near Navsari, Gujarat; go-live targeted FY29; technology partner talks ongoing.
Renewable power infrastructure: about Rs 3,250 crore committed; about 10 GW of grid connectivity, about 2 GW of PPAs (including 700 MW SECI FDRE), 25,000-30,000 acres of land under procurement.
demand_pricing: US pricing reset under Section 232: minimum import price of 38 cents/W plus 15% duty (about 44 cents landed) versus 27-28 cents landed today; realisation on US-made modules expected to rise from 26-27 cents toward 30-35 cents.

US-manufactured margin estimated at 8-9 cents/W at 70%+ utilisation (incl. about 7 cents/W incentive) versus about 3-4 cents/W EBITDA on exports from India; IRA incentives booked against dispatches and some sold.

India DCR module spot prices: utility 19-21 cents/W, retail 22-24 cents/W; forward FY28 prices 17.5-18.5 cents (utility) and 20-21 cents (retail). Non-DCR utility about 12-12.5 cents, retail 13.5-14 cents.
Management expects broad price correction in FY28 as capacity ramps across the industry; large integrated players expected to retain scale benefits.
Domestic module CUF fell to about 45% in Q2 as ALMM List-II extension shifted supply chains; management expects higher non-DCR volumes in Q3.
Indian demand (AC): residential plus C&I rooftop about 15 GW annualised; utility about 25 GW annualised; total about 55-60 GW DC per year per management.

qa_highlights.question: Retail channel economics: distributor margins, profitability, and how the distribution model is managed without visible opex increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Retail network is 775+ exclusive retail centres with about 3,000 distribution points and about 5,000 people; H1 retail revenue about Rs 5,700 crore, FY27 guided Rs 10,000-11,000 crore. Management cited operating leverage and partner growth (some partners from Rs 1-2 crore to Rs 50-75 crore a year), without giving channel margin figures.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further US order cancellations after the 2-2.5 GW deemed cancellations in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 3 GW-plus of export orders were stopped being reported, cutting export share of the order book from about 24% to 7.8%; US order book is rising. Post Section 232, US realisation is expected to rise from 26-27 cents to 30-35 cents per watt. Renegotiation into MIP-compliant contracts is ongoing for orders already dispatched but not yet recognised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic module CUF fall below 50% (about 45%) in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: ALMM List-II extension of about 6 months shifted supply chains and replanning took time, so non-DCR supply was delayed. Management expects non-DCR supply to rise and Q3 volumes to be higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall sequentially from 18.2% to 17.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 included a US duty refund; the refund rose from Rs 349 crore in Q1 to Rs 360.4 crore in Q2 (about Rs 11 crore booked in Q2). Like-for-like, margin improved with cell utilisation up from about 800 MW to over 1.1 GW per quarter and US module utilisation up from 60% to 70%+. Q3 and Q4 are expected to be heavy with 5 GW cell capacity each quarter plus US 1.6 GW lines; H2 expected at 55-60% of FY27 EBITDA guidance.

qa_highlights.question: US margin: how do exports from India compare with US-manufactured modules, and are IRA benefits included in reported numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Export from India yields about 3-4 cents/W EBITDA; US manufacturing gives about 2-3 cents operating margin at 70%+ utilisation plus about 7 cents/W incentive, so 8-9 cents/W total. Management said this is more than double export margins. IRA incentives are booked against dispatches and some are sold, so reported numbers include them.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic pricing: DCR and non-DCR prices and expected correction in FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: DCR spot: utility 19-21 cents/W, retail 22-24 cents/W; FY28 forward utility 17.5-18.5 cents and retail 20-21 cents. Non-DCR utility about 12-12.5 cents, retail 13.5-14 cents. Broad price correction expected in FY28, with scale players retaining benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiary (listed entity) EBITDA margins low relative to revenue of about Rs 22 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the listed subsidiary runs about 17-18% EBITDA standalone, but after acquiring a T&D entity (T&D margins about 10-11%) the blended margin is about 14-15%. T&D is lumpy, so the subsidiary is chasing larger order books.

qa_highlights.question: BESS, inverter and transformer revenue contribution in FY28 and margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Newer businesses expected to rise from 15-20% of revenue to 30-35% over 2-3 years; solar pure-play to 50-60% long range. Inverter and transformer EBITDA expected 18-22%; electrolyser 13-15%. Ballpark revenue from inverter, transformer and electrolyser about Rs 7,000-8,000 crore on about Rs 1,200 crore committed capital.

qa_highlights.question: Rs 1 lakh crore revenue ambition: how achievable and what split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 20-22 GW module output from the 29 GW solar PV base, realising about Rs 40,000-45,000 crore of solar revenue; with non-solar business and 75% utilisation, Rs 90,000-1 lakh crore within 4-5 years, with roughly equal module and non-module contribution. No firm timeline.

risks_watch: Further US order cancellations or renegotiations: about 2-2.5 GW deemed cancellations this quarter; export order share now 7.8%, and orders dispatched but not yet recognised are being renegotiated to MIP-compliant terms.

Execution of H2 ramp: H2 must deliver 55-60% of the Rs 7,000-7,700 crore FY27 EBITDA guidance; 5 GW India cell in Q3 and another 5 GW in Q4, plus US 1.6 GW lines in Q3 and Q4, must come online on time.

Q2 EBITDA dependence on US duty refund: refund was Rs 349 crore in Q1 and Rs 360.4 crore in Q2; reported margins include IRA incentives that management says are booked against dispatches and partly sold.
Pricing correction in FY28 as industry capacity rises (cell capacity close to 40 GW, heading to about 60 GW); DCR forward prices are 17.5-18.5 cents vs spot 19-21 cents.
Ingot-wafer plant at Nagpur (10 GW, commercial production targeted September 2027, capex about Rs 5,500 crore vs analyst's Rs 6,200-6,500 crore cited earlier); civil works about 70% complete.

Capex funding and balance sheet: Rs 30,000 crore programme (35% deployed, 28% under execution, 37% planning); large capital advances and rise in other current liabilities; BESS phase 2 funding tied to policy clarity and overseas orders.
Domestic CUF at about 45% in Q2 due to ALMM List-II extension; management expects higher non-DCR volumes in Q3.
key_quotes: We affirm our operating EBITDA guidance of Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,700 crores in FY '27.

So, partially yes, because the existing cell capacity is at around 81% in Q2, and considering the ramp-up which has already happened, I think we are at around 90% plus already running in the existing capacity.
So, H2 overall shall be around 55 % to 60% of the overall EBITDA guidance is what we are looking at.
We remain a net debt-free company with net cash of around Rs. 3,224 crores and a net debt-to-equity ratio of minus 0.2x.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, capacity and the Rs 1 lakh crore ambition, but cautious and somewhat evasive on US order cancellations, the sequential margin dip and the subsidiary's low margins. Several answers were given in ranges or directional terms with no firm numbers, and the order book was described as rationalised rather than cut.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of Rs 7,000-7,700 crore, with H2 needing about 55-60% of it (H1 about Rs 2,775 crore), backed by 5 GW Indian cell capacity going live in Q3 and another 5 GW in Q4, the US 1.6 GW line in Q3, and an order book of about Rs 59,200 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 17.8% (down from 18.2% in Q1, which included US duty refund); cell utilisation up from ~800 MW to 1.1 GW+ per quarter and US module utilisation 60% to 70%+, but FY28 price correction expected (DCR forward 17.5-18.5 cents vs spot 19-21 cents).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 5 GW Indian cell capacity going live in Q3 and another 5 GW in Q4, plus US 1.6 GW line in Q3 and a second 1.6 GW line next quarter; installed module capacity 25.8 GW with cell capacity 5.4 GW rising to 15.4 GW.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 module sales 3 GW (up 27%), management expects heavier Q3/Q4 volumes and higher non-DCR supply after domestic CUF fell to ~45%; order book ~Rs 59,200 crore with 25.6 GW module order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Cell utilisation ~81% in Q2 (management says ~90%+ now running) and the Rs 30,000 crore programme is only 35% deployed with 37% in planning; BESS Phase 2 (16.5 GWh cell) is in planning, funding tied to policy clarity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance only reaffirmed at Rs 7,000-7,700 crore; H2 must deliver 55-60% of it (H1 ~Rs 2,775 crore) and US export orders were cut from ~24% to 7.8% of the order book.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs roughly Rs 4,225-4,925 crore of EBITDA after H1 Rs 2,775 crore, depending on 5 GW cell lines in Q3 and Q4 and US lines coming on time; ~2-2.5 GW US deemed cancellations and ongoing renegotiations are a risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BESS pack (5.1 GWh) expected Q3, 3.5 GWh BESS cell pilot from Q4 FY27; inverter 4 GW production started and transformer incremental capacity by March 2027.

rows.label: US order book rationalised under Section 232
rows.why: Export share cut from ~24% to 7.8% of order book after ~3 GW of export orders stopped; US realisation expected to rise from 26-27 cents to 30-35 cents/W, but ongoing renegotiation of dispatched-but-unrecognised orders.

rows.label: FY28 industry price correction
rows.why: Management expects broad price correction in FY28 as capacity ramps (cell capacity near 40 GW heading to ~60 GW); DCR forward utility 17.5-18.5 cents vs spot 19-21 cents.

rows.label: Net cash position and self-funded capex
rows.why: Net cash about Rs 3,224 crore and management says cash covers under-construction projects without new borrowing; H1 operating cash flow about 5x prior full-year-equivalent.

tone.note: Management was confident on capacity ramps, the Rs 1 lakh crore ambition and reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA guidance, but cautious and somewhat evasive on US order cancellations, the sequential margin dip and subsidiary margins; analysts pushed on order book cuts and margin quality.
